findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "sml_discover" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Discover the SCRIPTMASTERLABS x402 Gateway contract (FREE, read-only). Returns the gateway's job, transport, and canonical payment contract — x402 v2, exact sch…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.detail: Description of "spend_gate_check" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: spend_gate_check, omnilist_run, omnilist_report · Private data: spend_gate_check, sml_xray_bars, omnilist_run · Public sink: precross_analyze, regime_scan_board, omnilist_report · Destructive: spend_gate_check, omnilist_run, omnilist_report, omnigate_runtime_execute, omnigate_runtime_receipt.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: spend_gate_check, omnilist_run, omnilist_report · Private data: spend_gate_check, sml_xray_bars, omnilist_run · Public sink: precross_analyze, regime_scan_board, omnilist_report · Destructive: spend_gate_check, omnilist_run, omnilist_report, omnigate_runtime_execute, omnigate_runtime_receipt

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "sml_discover" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
